sections.Overview:
Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites globally, offering a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products at low prices to generate high sales volume and rapid inventory turnover. The company's warehouses, averaging approximately 148,000 square feet, are designed for operational efficiency with no-frills, self-service formats that reduce labor and inventory costs. Costco's business model centers on efficient volume purchasing, streamlined distribution through cross-docking depots, and a limited SKU count (less than 4,000 SKUs per warehouse and 9,000 to 11,000 SKUs online) to sustain low costs and competitive pricing. The company also operates ancillary businesses such as gas stations, pharmacies, and travel services to complement core warehouse sales. Membership fees and renewal rates are significant, with 84.1 million paid members worldwide at the end of fiscal 2026 and a strong renewal rate of 92.3% in the US and Canada. Executive members, who pay an additional fee for rewards, accounted for 42.3 million memberships in 2026, contributing about 75.2% of worldwide net sales. The company's key operating regions include the US and Canada, representing a majority of sales and operating income. Costco emphasizes employee welfare as part of its ethics code and employs 355,000 people worldwide, mostly in warehouses and distribution. [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, L000733-L000783]

Insight: The company’s membership renewal rate excludes memberships expiring within six months prior to the reporting date, thereby potentially understating short-term renewal volatility; this nuanced membership accounting approach reflects careful management of reported membership stability [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, L000783] [C:membership_renewal_rate].
sections.Market Positioning and Growth Outlook: Costco's competitive positioning is grounded in its membership model, low price strategy enabled by volume purchasing, and efficient, large warehouse formats. The relatively narrow SKU selection reduces complexity and cost. The company operates in 17 countries including the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan, and several European and Asian nations. Its US and Canadian operations are critical, comprising 86% of net sales and 83% of operating income in fiscal 2026, with California alone making up 26% of US net sales. Costco's ancillary businesses, such as gas stations which contributed 11% of total net sales, add frequency and convenience for members. Growth catalysts include expanding warehouses primarily in existing markets, broadening e-commerce offerings, and developing private-label merchandise to increase member value. Challenges in growth include securing suitable new warehouse sites in competition with other retailers, regulatory constraints, and potential member cannibalization among warehouses. The company also seeks to diversify its supply chain and expand in-country sourcing. Digital sales growth is notable at 20.9% for fiscal 2026, indicating a significant e-commerce channel expansion. [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, L000733-L000783, L000834-L000841] [EX-99.1 accession 0000909832-26-000084, L000010-L000021]

sections.Future Developments and Strategic Recomm: Costco should continue to focus on expanding its warehouse footprint in both existing and new markets while managing risks related to site acquisition and regulatory compliance. Increasing the penetration of digitally-enabled sales and investing in e-commerce fulfillment will be key to capturing changing shopping behaviors. Enhancing private-label product offerings can improve margins and member loyalty. The company should monitor geographic and product concentration to mitigate operational risks, particularly given high dependence on US and Canadian operations and significant exposure to the California market. Maintaining high membership renewal rates through superior member value and reward programs will support steady revenue streams. Additionally, managing costs through operational efficiencies, including supply chain diversification and labor management, remains important. Monitoring international expansion performance and local market adaptation will inform future strategic moves. [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, L000733-L000783, L000834-L000841]

## Provisional Buy
The provisional Buy recommendation is supported primarily by the annual revenue growth of 10.14% for fiscal year 2026 [C:revenue_growth], evidencing strong top-line expansion which outweighs the moderate operating margin of 3.85%.

COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS
ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.
Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:

|  |  | Adjusted* |  |  |  | Adjusted*
U.S. | 10.7% |  | 7.2% |  | 8.2% |  | 6.6%

Other International | 7.0% |  | 6.2% |  | 9.8% |  | 6.5%
Total Company | 9.4% |  | 6.7% |  | 8.4% |  | 6.6%
Digitally-Enabled | 19.5% |  | 19.8% |  | 20.9% |  | 20.7%
*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange.
Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values. Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.
Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.
A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. (PT) today, September 24, 2026, and will be available via a webcast on investor.costco.com (click “Events & Presentations”).
